clue.text: "Misspoke" about Belgium, Israel labouring to become more enlightened

indicators.note: the first word's letters go around the rest, as about means surrounding

parts.note: someone who misspoke may simply have told a falsehood, i.e. lied
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

indicators.note: labouring suggests the letters of Israel are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician who misspoke about Belgium and Israel struggles to look more broad-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misspoke' in quotes hints at a euphemism for lying. B is the vehicle code for Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something liberalised has been made freer and less narrow-minded, i.e. it has become more enlightened.

clue.text: Excessive rise in Turkish currency left high rollers getting washed up here

definitions.text: high rollers getting washed up here

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the Turkish money

parts.note: the lira is the currency of Turkey

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise is read upwards, so these letters are turned back to front

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, i.e. excessive

explanation.surface: Gamblers lose out when the Turkish lira soars, and end up washed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High rollers' look like big-spending gamblers, but here they are large waves breaking on the shore. 'rise' turns OTT into TTO, which goes 'in' LIRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the littoral is the shore zone where big rolling waves are washed up.

clue.text: Bikini, for example, will go down very badly on location!

parts.note: a show that will bomb is one that will flop with its audience
a site is a location or place

explanation.surface: A skimpy swimsuit will be a disaster worn on a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is not the swimsuit but the Pacific atoll where the USA tested atomic bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bikini Atoll was a nuclear weapons test site, literally a place where bombs were exploded.

clue.text: On which Queen's speech might be gaga?

definitions.text: On which Queen's speech might be gaga?

parts.words: On which Queen's speech might be gaga
parts.note: the Queen's Christmas speech went out over the wireless

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch's address might ramble a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is both the monarch, whose Christmas speech is broadcast, and the rock band whose 1984 song is Radio Ga Ga.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the wireless set carries royal broadcasts and also names the Queen song Radio Ga Ga.

clue.text: Intros to heavy metal, fashionable at the start of the 70s

parts.note: lead is a famously heavy metal
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: the opening letter of the decade written out as a word is wanted

parts.note: the 70s are the seventies, spelt out

explanation.surface: Heavy metal bands, trendy in the early seventies, get their introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 70s' must be spelt out as SEVENTIES before its first letter, S, is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lead-ins are introductory passages, opening remarks or intros to something.

clue.text: Beach hotel squeezed in accommodation for one

indicators.note: the hotel letter is pressed into the middle of the room word

parts.note: a single is a room for one person
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A beachfront hotel crams guests into tiny single rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonym: shingle is a stony beach, so the word stands for the beach itself.

clue.text: Subtly nudge guy to acquire British sports car

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the extra letter into themselves
doing something subtly means in a roundabout way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gently persuade a chap to buy a British sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtly' rearranges NUDGE GUY, and 'to acquire' places B inside that new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dune buggy is a light open recreational car, a sporty vehicle for sand driving.

clue.text: Rabbit bone

definitions.meaning: in British slang to rabbit (on) is to chatter or talk at length
the mandible is the bone forming the lower face

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: chatter at length, as in British slang rabbiting on, and the hinged skull bone of the mouth.

clue.text: A hazard to swimmers in Skopje? Tsk! Infuriating!

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at the dangers awaiting bathers in Skopje, a landlocked city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of Skopje through Tsk to the I of Infuriating.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: personal watercraft zooming near bathers are a real danger to people in the water.

clue.text: Sally Ann issues this bloodcurdling scream

definitions.meaning: Sally Ann is slang for the Salvation Army
a battle shout yelled when charging into combat

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally Ann lets out a terrifying shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Salvation Army's long-running magazine title, and a fierce yell given in battle.

clue.text: Subdued, thanks to medicine

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A patient became calm thanks to the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an animal or rebel that is subdued has been brought under control.

clue.text: He turns away a poor relation

indicators.note: poor marks the word relation as badly formed, to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man snubs an impoverished member of his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He turns away' reads as a man averting his gaze, but describes someone who drives others off.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent noun: one who alienates others drives them off, making them turn away or estranging them.

clue.text: Ending foreign outsourcing of ordinary NHS groin surgery

indicators.note: surgery cuts up and rearranges, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The health service stops sending routine groin operations abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery' rearranges O, NHS and GROIN. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Business term: bringing work back home reverses offshoring, so it ends outsourcing to other countries.

clue.text: One reportedly peddling German ale laced with potassium

indicators.note: laced means spiked, so the element is mixed into the beer

parts.note: Bier is the German word for beer
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A dealer peddles German beer spiked with a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes peddling sound like pedalling, which is what a cyclist does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a cyclist or motorcyclist rider pedals, which sounds the same as peddling.

clue.text: It transports gold to America, billions on board

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so this letter goes within the others

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
US is America
B is short for billion(s)

explanation.surface: A vehicle ships gold to the USA with billions in its cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bus is a vehicle that transports passengers, and this is its fuller name.

clue.text: (Well qualified teacher concealing criminal conspiracy)

definitions.text: Well qualified teacher concealing criminal conspiracy

indicators.note: concealing means holding inside, so the conspiracy sits within the degree

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree held by a qualified teacher
a racket is an illegal scheme

explanation.surface: A trained teacher hides a criminal scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue sits in parentheses, i.e. it is itself enclosed in brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual joke: the clue is printed inside parentheses, so it is literally put in brackets, like the conspiracy inside the degree.

clue.text: Move gradually along narrow parapet, crumbling at the front

indicators.note: the ledge breaks away at its start, losing its first letter

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf or projecting rim

explanation.surface: A climber shuffles along a thin ledge that is falling away at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to edge along is to move slowly and carefully, inching forward.

clue.text: Record of Summer Holiday by Sandie Shaw broadcast; that'll show The White Stripes!

definitions.text: Record of Summer Holiday by Sandie Shaw broadcast; that'll show The White Stripes!

parts.words: Record of Summer Holiday by Sandie Shaw broadcast; that'll show The White Stripes
parts.note: skin browned by the sun at the seaside records a holiday, sandy shore spoken aloud evokes the coast, and strap marks leave pale stripes

explanation.surface: A radio show plays a pop singer covering the film song Summer Holiday, and namechecks a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer Holiday is a Cliff Richard song, Sandie Shaw a 1960s singer and The White Stripes a band, but the record here is the brown skin you bring home.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: sunbathing on sandy shores darkens skin, which records the trip and leaves pale stripes where straps were.

clue.text: No tears tenancy agreement?

definitions.meaning: rent means torn or a tear, so free of rents is without tears
a lease under which no payment is due

explanation.surface: A painless lettings deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: free of rents, i.e. tears, and an arrangement to occupy property without paying.

clue.text: Launder cash won for $100

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands in for another

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, and a C-note is a $100 bill
W is the abbreviation for the won, the Korean currency

explanation.surface: Clean up dirty money by swapping winnings for dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: The C of CASH is replaced by W.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to launder clothes is to clean them with water and soap.

clue.text: Sackcloth in ashes? That's wrong

indicators.note: saying the letters are wrong means they need putting right, in another order

explanation.surface: Someone questions the old phrase sackcloth and ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coarse jute or hemp fabric used for sacks is called sackcloth.

clue.text: Special rubber ring's new English hydrocarbon

parts.note: a tyre is a ring of rubber round a wheel

explanation.surface: A particular rubber ring is made from a new English chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this compound of carbon and hydrogen is used to make polystyrene and synthetic rubber.

clue.text: Because religious education's free from pretence

parts.note: since can mean because
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Faith lessons are honest because they are religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sincere person is genuine and honest, without any pretence.

clue.text: A coach fitted with air conditioning and a computer

indicators.note: fitted with means having inside, so the abbreviation goes within the vehicle

parts.note: a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A coach comes with air conditioning and an onboard computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer' is used in the old sense of a device for calculating.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the bead frame is an ancient calculating device, an early aid to computation.

clue.text: Dave turned up in North American state

indicators.note: in places the reversed name inside the abbreviation
in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, so the name is reversed

explanation.surface: Dave arrived in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives EVAD, which goes 'in' NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this is one of the fifty states of the USA, home to Las Vegas.

clue.text: A beach structure, Buddhist temple gets swamped by wave

indicators.note: swamped means engulfed, so the temple goes inside the wave

parts.note: a breaker is a large wave ... on the shore
a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A seaside temple is engulfed by a huge wave.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sea wall or barrier built out from a beach to shelter it from waves.

clue.text: I visited the Strand; it blew me away

definitions.text: I visited the Strand; it blew me away

parts.words: I visited the Strand; it blew me away
parts.note: the Strand sounds like London's street, but strand means beach, and a wind-driven land craft is blown along it

explanation.surface: A tourist raves about a trip to the Strand, the London street.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a wheeled sailing craft travels on the strand (beach), propelled by the wind.

clue.text: Yankee, consumed with dread, zigzagged at sea

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
awed means filled with fear and reverence

explanation.surface: A frightened American sailor steered an erratic course.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term: a ship that yaws swings off course from side to side.

clue.text: Cliff's here, social networking

indicators.note: the tail of the word networking, read on its own, says the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard is here, mingling at a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that 'networking' splits in two: its first three letters join SOCIAL as fodder and its last seven, 'working', are the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Location: cliffs are found along the shore, the boundary of land and sea.

clue.text: See 23
Assegai regularly chucked in the ocean

indicators.note: every other letter is thrown out, leaving a regular pattern of letters

explanation.surface: A spear is thrown repeatedly into the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: An assegai is a Zulu spear, so 'chucked' looks literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large body of salt water.

clue.text: Called in nerd Ancelotti to retain possession of the ball

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: A geek is called in for Ancelotti, the football manager, to keep possession of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlo Ancelotti is an Italian football manager; 'ball' here is a formal dance, not a football.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ball is a formal evening dance, often preceded by a meal.
